text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a challenge to supermarket competitor Coles Myer Ltd and the country's four big petrol retailers, Woolworths Ltd has forged a deal, worth A$750 million a year within five years, with Castrol's petroleum subsidiary Burmah Fuels and Japanese trading house Mitsui. Woolworths will buy fuel from Burmah Fuels' Singapore operations for a planned 200 retailing outlets around Australia. Page 1.

The Australian Institute of Company Directors said flaws in the Corporations Law are forcing larger companies to take commercial disputes to the courts after a survey of more than 600 company directors, conducted by the Institute and accountants KPMG, revaled that the larger a company becomes the more likely it is to take commercial disputes to the courts because a court-endorsed outcome is less risky for managers and directors. Page 3.

News Corp Ltd NCP.aX chairman Rupert Murdoch revealed yesterday at the company's annual meeting in Adelaide that News had A$3.38 billion in the bank, which would enable the company "to maintain liquidity" so it will be ready to take new opportunities as they arise. Page 19.

Boral Ltd managing director Tony Berg believes the company can achieve a price substantially above book value when it sells its Arkansas-based Briar Gypsum plasterboard business, which has a book value of A$58 million. Berg said the business would attract strong bidding as it is a low-cost operation.
Page 19.

Tourism operator Sydney Aquarium Ltd expects to attract at least another 200,000 to 300,000 Sydneysiders to its upgraded Darling Harbour site following an A$11 million extension of the marine centre, which will include a Barrier Reef exhibit and expanded estaurant and retail facilities. The company also predicts a 10 per cent increase in international tourists to Australia will boost attendance figures. Page 20.

At yesterday's annual general meeting in Perth, Western Australian publicly listed broking house Hartley Poynton Ltd announced a 94 per cent increase in net profits to A$1.8 million in its first quarter as a public company. Chairman Jock Clough said the result vindicated the board's decision earlier this year to undertake a A$10 million capital raising and listing. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

News Corp chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch told shareholders at the company's annual meeting in Adelaide that first quarter earnings for the group were below expectations, partly due to flat Australian newspaper earnings, but News would strive to make up the shortfall and still expected a 20 per cent rise in annual profit. Page 25.

News Corp chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch said yesterday the group would float some of its most significant digital technology interests - including News Datacom and the recently-purchased Digi-Media Vision - on the stock exchange, folding them into one company to be called Digital Media Services. Page 25.

As investors weighed into bank shares again following St George's A$2.65 billion takeover of Advance Bank Ltd on Monday, Wallis inquiry committee member Bill Beerworth said yesterday approval for bank mergers is likely to remain firmly in the hands of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission at the completion of the inquiry into the financial system. Page 25.

In a controversy stemming from the Federal Government's decision to limit the time frame in which the R&D concession could be claimed at the 150 per cent rate, Boral Ltd may act on legal advice that the Industry Research and Development Board was negligent in not registering claims lodged before a December 6 deadline last year - a move which could see the Federal Government facing a multi-million dollar bill from companies seeking the concession. Page 27.

The administrators of Digicall Group Ltd, which collapsed last month owing Vodafone Pty Ltd almost A$50 million, have told creditors that in the event of a liquidation they could pursue legal action against mobile phone carrier Vodafone (or its receiver) and Digicall directors. Page 27.

Struggling pay-TV operator Australis Media Ltd is confident it can repel threats of a fresh legal challenge from rival operator Foxtel. Australis is already being sued by Telstra Corp and News Limited - partners in Foxtel - over its infrastructure sharing agreement with Optus Vision, this time over voting rights at Monday's shareholder meeting in Sydney.
Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

News Corp chairman Rupert Murdoch told yesterday's annual general meeting in Adelaide that even though the group's profit growth in the first three months of 1997 was slower than expected, he still expects the international media group's annual profit to grow by 20 per cent this financial year, with the group "striving to make up any shortfall". Page 27.

In comments that will spark further speculation about the future of Australia's banking industry, Bill Beerworth, a key member of the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, told the annual Australian Society of CPA's congress yesterday he would not be concerned if Australia's four major banks became two mega-banks or if a foreigner bought out one of the big local banks. Page 27.

In a move mooted since 1994 when a A$400 million-plus float was flagged but then dumped, the AMP Society looks set to capitalise on the strong sharemarket and property market through a A$350 million listing of a portion of its A$6 billion property portfolo. Page 27.

St George Bank's share price rose 12 cents yesterday to A$8.67 as investors reacted positively to the bank's A$2.65 billion bid for Advance Bank, but some analysts were wary of the bank's ability to reduce annual expenses by 15 per cent or A$140 million in the next two-and-a-half years to make the deal pay. Page 29.

Casinos Austria International has offered Reef Casino Trust RCT.AX a A$6 million rental guarantee arrangement after Reef reported a A$5.9 million loss in the September quarter because of luckier-than-expected junket gamblers. Once the deal is finalised with the Queensland Government and the trustee, Casinos Austria will pay a first instalment of A$3 million, followed by a second A$3 million instalment in January 1997. Page 29.

According to the latest assessment by the Indicative Planning Council for the Housing Industry, new dwelling commencements this financial year will reach 127,000, only slightly above last year's 124,550. This indicates another tough year for the housing ndustry, but the council forecasts next financial year will improve, with 142,000 commencements. Page 29.
THE AGE

Addressing News Corporation's annual meeting in Adelaide yesterday, Rupert Murdoch told shareholders the company's profit growth in the first three months of this financial year was slower than expected, however he said he still expected the international media group's annual profit to grow by 20 per cent in 1996-97. Page C1.

In a frank address to the annual Association of Certified Practising Accountants congress yesterday, Bill Beerworth, an influential member of the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, revealed he would not be concerned if Australia's four big banks were reduced to two mega-banks, or if a foreigner bought out one of the major local banks. Page C1.

Dutch telecommunications and postal giant KPN yesterday stepped up its takeover campaign by buying almost 30 million shares in transport and logistics group TNT at between A$2.42 and A$2.45, bringing TNT to its foreign ownership threshold of 15 per cent. KPN must now await Foreign Investment Review Board approval to proceed with its offer for TNT. Page C1.

A national survey prepared for the Institute of Chartered Accountants indicates Australian companies are out of touch when it comes to knowing what investors want to read in annual reports, and most do not provide information on environmental issues - an area important for investors, stockbrokers and shareholders. Page C3.

The rationalisation of the Adelaide Steamship group took another step forward yesterday when Adsteam and its affiliate Tooth & Co sold their remaining 37.3 million shares, or a 19 per cent stake, in building and construction group National Consolidated. Asteam and Tooth raised A$32.1 million and A$6.8 million respectively from the sale of their combined stake. Page C3.

According to a draft prospectus, Australia's first listed infrastructure trust, Macquarie Bank's Infrastructure Trust of Australia Group, intended to raise A$400 million in two instalments, attracting investors with an expected 10.4 per cent annualised cash yield from the offer's close to the end of the 1996-97 year. However, this could be replaced with a single A$300 million raising which may offer an even higher annualised yield. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
